description: Attempted to toggle nanoex off (from true, confirmed matching the app) while Kevin had the official app open checking current Cooling/NanoeX state (view only, confirmed no changes made in-app). Rejected -- new error code, apparent 2-minute lockout of unclear origin (see corrected notes).

error.message: 他の機器でエアコンが制御されました。2分間変更できません。
error.message_en_approx: The air conditioner was controlled by another device. Cannot be changed for 2 minutes.

notes: Third distinct E-21291-* code seen this session (after 00002 clock-skew, and 00007/01712 generic-application-error family). This one has a specific, actionable message rather than a generic apology.

RE-CONFIRMED theory, now with solid evidence: it IS a cross-client write conflict. Kevin reports the official app fires a real PUT ('writing settings' modal) just from opening and closing the NanoeX menu, even with zero value change -- so even though he never changed anything, the app itself still wrote. That write (from the app, a different client) is almost certainly what put the appliance into the 2-minute lockout that then rejected our CLI's write. The earlier 'self-cooldown from our own prior write' correction was wrong -- reverting to the original cross-client-lockout theory, now confirmed rather than guessed.

Real implication for the HA integration: this is a genuine risk whenever the official app (or presumably the physical remote) is used around the same time as HA -- even just opening a menu in the app without changing anything can lock HA out of writing for ~2 minutes. Should map this code to a distinct exception (e.g. EoliaDeviceLockedError) with a 'try again shortly, another client just changed this device' message rather than a generic HomeAssistantError. A coordinator-side minimum-interval-between-writes safeguard would NOT fully prevent this, since the trigger is external (the app), not our own write cadence.
Did NOT retry immediately -- waiting out the ~2 minute window before re-attempting the nanoex toggle, to avoid hammering the endpoint during an active lockout.
